seoDescription: Compare auto repair marketing agencies for independent shops. See which channels bring the most jobs, what to expect and what to ask before you hire.
content:
Quick answer: The best auto repair marketing agency works with independent shops today, runs Google Ads, local search and review campaigns together, and reports booked repair orders instead of clicks. Before you hire, check who owns your accounts, how long the contract runs and what the fee covers.

Key Takeaways

Repair shops get most new customers from Google: search ads, the map results and reviews. A good agency runs those channels together and adds service reminders to bring customers back. Many big names in automotive marketing mainly serve car dealerships, so check whether an agency works with independent shops like yours. Ask for examples, find out who owns your Google and ad accounts, and get the fee and ad spend in writing. Expect setup and tracking in the first month and a clear report on calls and booked jobs by the third.

What an Auto Repair Marketing Agency Does

An auto repair marketing agency runs the channels that bring cars into your bays, so you can focus on the shop. That usually means Google Ads, your Google Business Profile, review requests, your website and service reminders. A done-for-you agency handles the work and sends you reports. A do-it-yourself plan keeps the work in-house and relies on your own time and tools. An independent shop and a dealer service department need different things. A dealer service department can lean on the dealership's brand, inventory traffic and manufacturer programs. An independent shop has to win each customer through local search, reviews and a clear offer.

If you only need better rankings, compare auto repair SEO companies instead. Ads, reviews and reminders tend to work best when one team runs them together.

How We Picked These Auto Repair Marketing Agencies

We used six criteria. We checked each one against what the agency says it offers.
  • Independent shop clients: Does it work with independent shops today?
  • Channels offered: Does it cover ads, local search, reviews and your website?
  • Booked-job tracking: Does it report booked repair orders?
  • Contract and account ownership: Do you own your Google and ad accounts?
  • Pricing clarity: Is the fee separate from ad spend?
  • Proof: Does it have industry association ties or published case studies?

1. ITZ Digital: Ads, Local Search and Websites for Repair Shops

Best for: Shops that want ads, local search and a website from one team. ITZ Digital is our own agency, so weigh this profile with that in mind. It runs Google Ads, local SEO and review campaigns for repair shops, and builds shop sites through its website design service. Its reporting is built around calls and booked jobs rather than clicks. See what shops spend in our auto repair marketing costs guide.

2. DealerOn: Websites and Marketing for Dealerships

Best for: Dealership service departments. DealerOn mainly provides website platforms and digital marketing to car dealerships. It offers website design, SEO, paid search and social media management. An independent shop will find that most of its tools are built around dealership sales.

3. Dealer.com: A Full Suite for Dealership Groups

Best for: Large dealership groups with a service department. Dealer.com is a Cox Automotive brand. It offers websites, digital advertising and managed services for dealerships. Service departments inside a dealership group can use it, but it is aimed at dealers rather than independent repair shops.

4. Automotive Marketing Solutions: Details to Confirm First

Best for: Shops that are willing to check details directly. We could not find independent sources that confirm what Automotive Marketing Solutions offers or who it serves. Ask for client references, a list of services and a sample report before you sign anything.

5. J&L Marketing: Direct Mail and Digital

Best for: Shops that want direct mail paired with digital campaigns. J&L Marketing started in direct mail and event marketing for the automotive industry and has added digital services. That mix can suit shops that still get customers from mailers and local promotions.

6. NetDriven: Websites for Independent Shops

Best for: Independent repair shops and tire dealers. NetDriven builds websites and online marketing for independent repair shops and tire dealers. Internet Brands bought the company in 2015, so it is part of the Internet Brands automotive group. It is the one agency here built mainly for independent shops.

7. AutoRevo: Inventory Tools and Digital Marketing

Best for: Dealership groups with a service department. AutoRevo sells inventory management, website and digital marketing tools, mostly to dealerships. Its marketing tools can reach a dealership's service department, but its core strength is vehicle sales.

What to Expect in Your First 90 Days With an Agency

  • Month 1: The agency audits your accounts, sets up call and booking tracking, and fixes your Google Business Profile.
  • Month 2: Ads go live and your service pages are built or improved.
  • Month 3: You get a first report on calls and booked jobs.
No agency can promise results in this window. Judge the first 90 days by how clear the tracking and reporting are.

Questions to Ask Before You Hire

Ask every agency these six questions first.
  • Which independent shops do you work with today?
  • Who owns the Google and ad accounts?
  • How long is the contract, and how do I leave?
  • How do you report booked jobs?
  • What is the fee, and what is the ad spend on top of it?
  • Who will be my contact person?

faqs.question: What does an auto repair marketing agency do?
faqs.answer: It runs the marketing that brings cars into your bays, such as Google Ads, your Google Business Profile, reviews, your website and service reminders. A good one reports booked repair orders, not just clicks.

faqs.question: What is the best digital marketing agency for an independent auto repair shop?
faqs.answer: One that works with independent shops today, not mainly dealerships, and tracks booked jobs. Compare the options above against the six points in our criteria.

faqs.question: How much does an auto repair marketing agency cost?
faqs.answer: Agencies charge a monthly fee, and ad spend is paid on top. SEO alone for a repair shop often runs $1,000 to $3,000 a month. Ask for a written quote that separates the two.

faqs.question: How long before I see results?
faqs.answer: Google Ads can bring calls within weeks. SEO and reviews build over three to six months.

faqs.question: Should I hire an SEO company or a full-service agency?
faqs.answer: If you only need better rankings, an SEO company fits; see our auto repair SEO company comparison. If you need ads, reviews and reminders too, a full-service agency is simpler.
